result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edge clustering coefficient for specified edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10484-L10617){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient( edge_ids=None, k=3, normalize=True, offset=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The edge clustering coefficient measures how "clustered" the neighborhood around an edge is, based on k-cycles (cycles of length k) the edge participates in. For `k=3` (triangles): - counts triangles containing the edge - maximum possible: `min(d_i - 1, d_j - 1)` where `d_i`, `d_j` are endpoint degrees - value of `1.0` means edge is in a complete subgraph For `k=4` (4-cycles): - counts 4-cycles containing the edge - maximum possible: `(d_i - 1)(d_j - 1)` - measures "squareness" of edge neighborhood ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of edge IDs (integers) to compute coefficient for. If `None`, computes for all edges. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Cycle size to use. Must be `3` (triangles) or `4` (4-cycles). [normalize]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to normalize by maximum possible cycles given endpoint degrees. If `False`, returns raw cycle count. [offset]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to add `1` to cycle count (original Radicchi et al. definition). When `offset=True`: `C(e) = (z + 1) / s`. When `offset=False`: `C(e) = z / s`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mapping from edge ID (integer) to clustering coefficient. With `normalize=True`: range `[0, 1+]` (can exceed `1` with offset). With `normalize=False`: raw cycle count. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If k is not 3 or 4. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Radicchi et al. (2004) introduced this metric to identify community-bridging edges: edges embedded in many short cycles are internal to a community, while those embedded in few are candidates for removal in Girvan-Newman-style algorithms. Their original definition uses `normalize=True` and `offset=True`, which adds $1$ to the raw cycle count so a score of $0$ never appears; setting `offset=False` recovers the more natural convention where an edge inside a complete subgraph scores exactly $1$. Runtime is $O(|V|\,d\log d + |E|\,d)$ for $k=3$ (triangles) and $O(|V|\,d\log d + |E|\,d^2)$ for $k=4$ (4-cycles), where $d$ is the maximum degree. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every edge of a triangle sits in exactly one triangle, and with `offset=True` (the default) that count is bumped by one before dividing by the maximum possible: ::: {#25356a3e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, normalize=True, offset=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {2: 2.0, 3: 2.0, 1: 2.0} ``` ::: ::: Setting `offset=False` lets a fully-clustered edge reach the natural maximum of `1.0`: ::: {#8e7e1429 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, normalize=True, offset=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {2: 1.0, 3: 1.0, 1: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: A 4-cycle has no triangles at all, so `k=3` clustering is zero everywhere, but each edge does participate in exactly one 4-cycle, so `k=4` gives every edge a value of `1.0`: ::: {#a020cf6f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("D", "A") ) graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, offset=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {3: 0.0, 1: 0.0, 4: 0.0, 2: 0.0} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#623bdf1a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=4, offset=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {3: 1.0, 1: 1.0, 4: 1.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: On a real network like the karate club, sorting by clustering surfaces the edges most embedded in triangles: ::: {#1f58eea7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.karate_club() ecc = G.get_edge_clustering_coefficient(k=3, normalize=True, offset=False) sorted_edges = sorted(ecc.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) sorted_edges[:5] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` [(50, 1.0), (56, 1.0), (68, 1.0), (49, 1.0), (11, 1.0)] ``` ::: :::
